mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a quarterly GDPC1 decline exceeding 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based recovery in demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise > 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate above 4.5% (from a lower baseline) signals an aggressive tightening stance, which quickly raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps above 4.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative after a single-month FEDFUNDS jump above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is inconsistent with normal labor market dynamics and signals a data anomaly or severe shock, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both rise > 0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS rise > 0.3pp in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals a persistent supply-side contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and raises recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative following three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) combined with a stable CPI (CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2%) signals robust demand growth with low inflation, which supports earnings and justifies positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 2% and CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises > 2% and CPIAUCSL change is within ±0.2% in the same month.
